text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic says he does not believe Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's politics are good for the future of the Serb people, Serbia and Yugoslavia in an interview with weekly Vreme.
- The three member parties of Zajedno coalition sign agreements on joint bodies and participation in presidential and parliamentary elections.
- Belgrade municipal council to be constituted today, as special law on local elections reinstating November 17 opposition victory comes into effect.
- Belgrade university deans insist on resignation of rector Dragutin Velickovic as condition to resume classes.
- Workers of electrical industry from Nis EI-NIS threaten to go on general strike unless an extraordinary session of the managing board is held on Friday.
- Yugoslav and Italian shoe factories Kostana and Carmens sign five-year 80 million German mark deal.
- Serbia has more independent media than the U.S. and European countries, Serbia's new Information Minister Radmila Milentijevic tells reporters in New York.
- Some 30 percent of Belgrade pre-schools reopen on Friday, others still remain closed pending talks with new city government.
- Federal Interior Minister Vukasin Jokanvic appointed president of the managing board of Radio TV Serbia replacing Serbian culture minister Nada Popovic Perisic who resigned.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslavia buys 20 Massey Ferguson tractors on a five-year credit and is negotiating for 50 more.
- Joint claims of the Serbian electricity company and oil industry EPS and NIS total 3.8 billion dinars ($680 million).

- Serbian government rejects striking teachers' proposals. Unless schools reopen on February 24, the government said it would implement all its constitutional rights and replace teachers who do not return to work by Wednesday.
BORBA
- New management of radio TV Kragujevac puts up a list of 42 employees to be sacked.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Talks on calming Kosovo tensions are not and will not be led under pressure from the United States or any other factors, Yugoslav Left vice president Aleksandar Vulin says.

- The provincial government of Vojvodina, Yugoslavia's breadbasket, will ask the Serbian government to insist with the National Bank on a 3-5 year freeze on repayment of farm credits and on stable sources of funds for financing spring sowing.
- Spring sowing to begin in ten days, still unclear how the 800 million dinars debt to farmers will be settled.
-- Belgrade newsroom, 381 11 222 4305
